data.name: Israfil
data.gender_notes: Israfil is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Israfil is an angel mentioned in the Quran. He is believed to blow the trumpet that will mark the beginning of the Day of Resurrection. The name Israfil carries the meaning “The Angel of the Trumpet” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Israfil usually hope their child will grow to embody the angel of the trumpet and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine judgment and the arrival of the Day of Judgment.
data.etymology: Israfil belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Angel of the Trumpet.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Israfil total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_english.name: Israfil
in_english.meaning: Leader of the Angels, Angel of Judgment, Bringer of Death, Angel of Resurrection
in_english.long_meaning: Israfil is the leader of the angels, the angel of judgment, the bringer of death, and the angel of resurrection. He is the angel who will blow the horn of judgment, signaling the end of the world, and the beginning of the day of resurrection. Israfil is also known as the angel of death, who will take the souls of the righteous to heaven, and the souls of the wicked to hell. He is considered one of the most important angels in Islam, and is often depicted as a powerful and majestic figure.

The concept of a messianic figure blowing a trumpet to announce the end of the world is found in various religious and mythological traditions around the world, and Israfil represents this idea in the Islamic context. He also plays a significant role in Islamic art and literature, and is often depicted blowing his trumpet or carrying it.
data.spiritual_significance: Israfil is considered the herald of the Day of Judgment, and his blowing of the trumpet is seen as a call for all beings, living and dead, to gather before God for the final reckoning. The idea of the Day of Judgment is a powerful one in Islamic beliefs, and the figure of Israfil represents both the fearsome power and the irresistible call of God. The trumpet blast is also seen as a reminder of the transience of worldly life and the importance of preparing spiritually for the journey to the next life.
